review_notes: I read the whole file and checked Mathlib's Order/Ideal.lean and Order/Completion.lean for an existing lemma saying an ideal is the supremum of the principal ideals of its elements. I found none. The finsetSup_mem_iff calls recur but each has different parameters, so I did not report them. I did not compile the proposed rewrite, so the exact tactic details are unconfirmed.

findings.problem: Both proofs prove that an ideal I is the supremum of the principal ideals of its elements: `sSup (principal '' (I : Set A)) = I`. Lines 155–161 prove it as `hsSup`, and lines 175–180 repeat the same `le_antisymm` argument inside the instance. Both blocks use the same `sSup_le` step with `principal_le_iff` and the same `mem_of_mem_of_le mem_principal_self (le_sSup ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)` step. The same set `S := principal '' (I : Set A)` is also built separately in each proof. The fact has no name, so a reader cannot see that the two proofs depend on one result. A change to the argument would have to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Before `isCompactElement_iff_eq_principal`, add:

`theorem sSup_principal_image (I : Ideal A) : sSup (principal '' (I : Set A)) = I := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact sSup_le (by rintro _ ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩; exact principal_le_iff.mpr ha)
  · intro a ha
    exact mem_of_mem_of_le mem_principal_self (le_sSup ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)`

This is the current proof text moved into a lemma. Then use it in both places.

In `isCompactElement_iff_eq_principal`, replace the `hsSup` block with `have hsSup : sSup S = I := sSup_principal_image I`.

In the instance, use `exists_sSup_eq I := ⟨principal '' (I : Set A), by rintro _ ⟨a, _, rfl⟩; exact isCompactElement_principal a, sSup_principal_image I⟩`.

The lemma needs no new imports or hypotheses. It uses only `[DistribLattice A] [BoundedOrder A]`, which are already in the section variables, plus `Order.Ideal`'s existing `principal_le_iff`, `mem_principal_self` and `sSup_le`.
findings.benefit: The shared density fact, that every ideal is the join of its principal ideals, gets a name and one proof. Both consumers shrink to a single line. The instance reads as "principal ideals are compact and generate". Any later change to how `sSup` of ideals is characterized has to be fixed in one place only.
